name: Charles B. Mikell III, MD
identity: Associate Professor and Vice Chair, Department of Neurosurgery, Stony Brook University / Renaissance School of Medicine (Stony Brook, NY). Functional and epilepsy neurosurgeon; joined Stony Brook in 2016.
bio: Charles Mikell is a functional neurosurgeon at Stony Brook who treats epilepsy, movement disorders (Parkinson's, essential tremor, dystonia), spasticity, chronic pain, and brain tumors, using deep brain stimulation, stereo-EEG, and minimally invasive approaches. He came to Stony Brook from Columbia in 2016 and has built a program spanning functional, epilepsy, and tumor neurosurgery, rising to Vice Chair. His research centers on disorders of consciousness and return of consciousness after brain injury, cognitive-control mechanisms in the frontal lobe, and clinical trials for glioblastoma. He is an active academic surgeon with publications in high-impact venues (Nature Neuroscience, Stroke) and a substantial citation record.
training: Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians & Surgeons (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, Columbia University / NewYork-Presbyterian · Functional neurosurgery fellowship, University of Louisville · Pedigree note: trained in the Columbia functional/epilepsy group (McKhann/Sheth/Schevon), strong disorders-of-consciousness and human electrophysiology research lineage.
litt_exposure: Claims signal shows LITT performance (litt_perf = 5) in the 'LITT — Our Equipment (NeuroBlate)' cohort, alongside SEEG (8) and epilepsy craniotomy (10) volume, consistent with an active NeuroBlate user for epilepsy/tumor ablation. Web sources confirm his epilepsy, functional, and tumor practice but do not independently name a specific LITT platform, so brand attribution rests on the claims cohort.
wheelhouse: Epilepsy surgery (SEEG-guided), functional neurosurgery (DBS for Parkinson's/tremor/dystonia), disorders of consciousness, brain tumors including glioblastoma. LITT fits his epilepsy and deep-tumor practice.
kol_note: Academic thought leader in functional neurosurgery and disorders of consciousness (Vice Chair; Nature Neuroscience / Stroke publications; well-cited). His KOL standing is in DBS/consciousness/epilepsy neurophysiology rather than specifically in LITT.

name: David A. Chesler, MD, PhD
identity: Director of Pediatric Neurosurgery and Clinical Associate Professor of Neurosurgery and Pediatrics, Stony Brook University / Renaissance School of Medicine (Stony Brook, NY). Board-certified pediatric neurosurgeon (FAANS, FAAP); joined Stony Brook in 2014.
bio: David Chesler directs pediatric neurosurgery at Stony Brook Children's and is one of the few pediatric neurosurgeons in Suffolk County. His clinical focus includes minimally invasive endoscopic repair of craniosynostosis, pediatric and adult epilepsy surgery, brain and spinal cord tumors, and cerebral revascularization for moyamoya disease. He is an MD/PhD with a research background in cerebral ischemia/edema and more than 50 publications. His pediatric-and-adult epilepsy and tumor practice places him squarely in the clinical territory where LITT is used, though the claims data classifies him as a LITT-naïve craniotomy surgeon.
training: Albert Einstein College of Medicine of Yeshiva University (MD, PhD) · Neurosurgery residency (not independently verified) · Pediatric Neurosurgery fellowship, Johns Hopkins · Pedigree note: Johns Hopkins pediatric neurosurgery training; MD/PhD research background in cerebral ischemia/edema.
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Claims cohort is 'LITT-Naïve Craniotomy Surgeon' with SEEG (2), epilepsy craniotomy (5), and mets/RN (10) volume but no LITT procedures. Web sources describe open/endoscopic and vascular practice, with no mention of laser ablation.
wheelhouse: Pediatric neurosurgery; endoscopic craniosynostosis repair; pediatric and adult epilepsy surgery; brain and spinal cord tumors; moyamoya revascularization.
kol_note: Regional leader in pediatric neurosurgery on Long Island (department director, FAANS/FAAP, 50+ publications) but not a national LITT thought leader. Craniosynostosis and pediatric epilepsy are his visible niches.

candidacy.rationale: He performs exactly the case mix that drives LITT adoption — pediatric and adult epilepsy surgery plus brain tumor work — yet is LITT-naïve, and Stony Brook already runs NeuroBlate through Mikell, giving an in-house platform and champion to onboard him. Pediatric epilepsy (mesial temporal, hypothalamic hamartoma, tubers) and deep/small tumors are premier NeuroBlate indications. His demonstrated adoption of other minimally invasive intracranial technologies (Apollo, endoscopic craniosynostosis) suggests receptivity. Modest SEEG/epilepsy craniotomy volume in the claims means the epilepsy pipeline exists but is not yet large; growth potential is real but should be sized against actual candidate volume.

name: Alexander Winkler-Schwartz, MD, PhD
identity: Neurosurgeon at Stony Brook University Hospital (Stony Brook, NY); Director of the Skull Base Tumor Center and Associate Director of the Cerebrovascular Center, with dual pediatric neurosurgery and skull-base/neuro-oncology training. Not present in the claims dataset (in_claims = false; NPI not provided).
bio: Alexander Winkler-Schwartz is a McGill-trained neurosurgeon whose practice spans neuro-oncology, skull-base surgery, cerebrovascular surgery, and pediatric brain tumors across all ages. He holds a PhD in neuroscience from McGill's Neurosurgical Simulation and Artificial Intelligence Learning Centre (NeuroSim), where he became a leading contributor to machine-learning assessment of surgical expertise in virtual-reality simulation, with publications in JAMA Network Open and recognition via a Canadian Brain Star Award. He completed a sequence of subspecialty fellowships (skull base/cerebrovascular, pediatric neuro-oncology, pediatric neurosurgery) before joining Stony Brook. His tumor-heavy, multi-age practice overlaps meaningfully with LITT indications, but there is no evidence he currently performs laser ablation.
